findings.reason: §2 should resolve the section through `reckon/crew/routing.py:section_record_id` (or state why the predicate may accept a narrower grammar) so a section has one identity, which is the whole point of the existing owner.
findings.text: `followup_pointers.parse_invocation` normalises the section with its own regex (`_INVOCATION_RE`, `f"s{number}"` at reckon/followup_pointers.py:87) instead of resolving through `section_record_id`, the existing owner of section identity, so the predicate and the owner disagree on non-simple spellings: `/reckon-build <plan> §1-2` yields `s1` from the predicate but `§1-2`/`s1-2` from the owner, and `§2a` yields `s2a` versus the owner's unparsed `§2a`; since §2 judges the section against `<meta name="plan-section-declarations">` keys (confirmed `s1`,`s2`,… in the served snapshot), a followup whose section spelling is not the simple `§N` is misclassified as hiding or pointing

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `reckon/followup_pointers.py` hides the invocation regex, plan-ref resolution, host-complete precedence and the `section_declarations` lookup behind one `classify_followup` and a fixed reason vocabulary (`HIDING_REASONS`/`POINTER_REASONS`), so roadmap and the write path consume one answer.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the predicate re-derives a plan section identity (`§N` → `sN`) that `reckon/crew/routing.py:215` `section_record_id` already owns ("the one identity every spelling of a plan section addresses"), and the two derivations disagree.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan's §1 surveys the two places followups are read (`continuation_present` in `reckon/_store.py`, `_dispatchability` in `reckon/roadmap.py`), and the implemented predicate reuses `parse_plan_ref` (`reckon/_schema.py:274`), `COMPLETED_STATUSES` (`reckon/_store` lifecycle) and the roadmap's `_finding`/`wiring_findings` aggregate rather than rebuilding them.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §3's refusal is built on the shared predicate (`_refuse_hiding_followup`, `reckon/_store.py:3217`) and wired into the existing write boundary already owned by `_store.py` (the append op and `validate_landing_patch`), not a parallel classifier.
